result.summary: Ignore BIP35 mempool messages from peers that have transaction relay disabled (fRelay=false), unless the connection has the mempool net permission. Peers can still obtain mempool inventory after enabling transaction relay, such as by sending a BIP37 filterload message, which subjects them to existing inbound transaction-relay connection limits.
result.problem: When a node runs with bloom filtering enabled, an inbound peer can connect with fRelay=false to evade the inbound transaction-relay connection capacity limits introduced in PR 28463, while still requesting and receiving full mempool inventory via BIP35 mempool messages.
evidence: PR description: 'When a node offers NODE_BLOOM, an inbound peer can advertise fRelay=false and request BIP35 mempool inventory while remaining outside the inbound transaction-relay capacity introduced in #28463.'

Commit 3e64b65359: 'An inbound peer with fRelay=false stays outside transaction-relay capacity accounting, yet BIP35 requests give it full mempool inventory. Ignore these requests until transaction relay is enabled, except when the operator grants the mempool permission.'
result.changed_since_previous: The implementation remains the same; release notes and an entry in doc/bips.md documenting the behavior for v33.0 were added.
result.card: Bitcoin Core now ignores BIP35 mempool requests from peers that have transaction relay disabled, unless they are granted the mempool network permission. Currently, inbound peers can connect with fRelay=false to avoid counting toward the inbound transaction-relay capacity limit added in PR 28463, yet still consume bandwidth by requesting full mempool inventory. Requiring active transaction relay closes this loophole while preserving SPV clients like bitcoinj that send a BIP37 filterload message before requesting the mempool.

risk.why: A flaw in P2P message processing could inadvertently disconnect or drop valid inventory requests from legitimate SPV clients or peers with custom permissions.
